title: Only one man in Vrindavan
hookLine: a holy man in Vrindavan won't meet a woman, and Mira's one sentence teaches how the soul stands before Krishna
carry: before krishna, the soul is the beloved
last: BHAKTI IS LOVE YOU CAN HEAR.

cards: A door, and a message passed through it. On one side, a learned renunciant in Vrindavan who has made a rule for himself: he doesn't meet women.

On the other, a woman who has walked a long way to see him, and has just been turned away. She doesn't argue about the rule. She sends back a single sentence, and by the end of the story, the door opens.
The woman is Mira, and the sentence is today's whole lesson.

teach.b: Tradition says that after the troubles with her husband's family, Mira left the palace and took to the road, and came to Vrindavan, the country of Krishna's childhood, where the cowherd girls, the gopis, once ran to the sound of his flute.

teach.h: A HOLY MAN WHO WON'T MEET WOMEN
teach.b: Holy people and teachers lived there. The story names one of them as Jiva Goswami, a scholar of Krishna devotion; some tellings name another teacher. The story, in paraphrase: Mira asks to meet him.
Word comes back that he has vowed not to see women.
And Mira answers, roughly: I thought there was only one man in Vrindavan, Krishna. I didn't know anyone else here was claiming to be a man. The renunciant hears it, and comes out to meet her.

It's sharp, and it's funny. But under the wit is a teaching that belongs to Vrindavan itself. In the devotion Vrindavan is known for, the soul stands before Krishna the way the gopis did: as the beloved, waiting for him.
Before him, no one is the man of the house. That's why poets of this devotion, men included, so often sing in a gopi's voice.
So the rule that kept her out rested on a difference that, in that place, she says doesn't count. And she doesn't attack his vow, or his learning, or him.
She takes the faith of the place more seriously than the rule does, and lets that speak. Last, this isn't a record anyone wrote down at the door.
It's one of the stories told about her, remembered because it teaches, the way a parable does.

how: Vrindavan remains a place of pilgrimage for Krishna devotees, and stories of Mira's time there are told alongside her songs in bhajan gatherings.

o: a poet who opened a closed door with one sharp line
a poet who broke a holy man's vow by force of argument
a poet who was turned away and left Vrindavan for good

p: has vowed not to meet women
the cowherd girls who loved Krishna

she leaves his learning alone and answers from the faith of the place.

games.q: you're Mira. you've walked to Vrindavan, and a holy man sends word that he doesn't meet women. what do you do?
o: send back that there's only one man in Vrindavan.
wait outside until he gives in.
games.why: she answers that she thought Krishna was the only man in Vrindavan, and the renunciant comes out to meet her.

practice: Notice the labels you carry today: your job, your role at home, how others see you. Name one quietly, then on an out-breath set it down beside you like a bag.

For a few breaths, stand the way the gopis stood before Krishna: no title, only someone who loves and is loved. If you pray, stand before God that way for a moment. If you don't, just be someone breathing.

wordCard.voice: Mirabai. Turned away in Vrindavan by a holy man who wouldn't meet women, she answered that there was only one man there, Krishna.

orig.note: Sanskrit and Hindi: Vrindavan, the land of Krishna's childhood, where tradition says Mira came.

carryVoice: Your line: before krishna, the soul is the beloved. Mira said it at a closed door. Rest well.
